key_insight: Engineered surfaces require hierarchical, multi-modal NDE that pairs rapid screening with calibrated confirmation tailored to surface and interface properties.
engineering_relevance: Matching inspection physics to coating thickness, adhesion, residual stress, porosity, and debonding can support quality control and service-life assessment.
method: Review electromagnetic, thermal, acoustic, optical, and X-ray inspection capabilities and limitations.
Link NDE methods to defects in coatings, cold-sprayed deposits, clad overlays, and other engineered surfaces.
Assess in-process sensing, data fusion, physics-informed machine learning, and digital twins for NDE 4.0.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a methods review, not a new experimental benchmark, and highlights limited probability-of-detection evidence.
watch_item: Qualification remains constrained by scarce reference specimens, incomplete acceptance criteria, and poor transferability of data-driven models.
paper_title: Non-Destructive Evaluation for Engineered Surfaces: Methods, In-Process Sensing, and Data-Driven Inspection in the NDE 4.0 Era
